widgets.title: Why it works:
widgets.description: A subscription is a promise repeated every month. The hero states the promise; the next block shows what actually arrives, so the price that follows has something to be compared with.

widgets.title: What subscribers get, every month

items.title: A delivery with a rhythm
items.description: Say what arrives and when: "a new template pack on the first Monday". Predictability is what people pay for monthly.

items.title: Access that accumulates
items.description: The library, the archive, the community: things that grow while the subscription runs and make leaving cost something.

items.title: A first win in the first week
items.description: Describe what a new subscriber achieves before the second charge. If you cannot name it, churn starts there.

widgets.content:
Sell the second month

Anyone can sell the first month. Describe the value in a way that still makes sense in month six, and the page will attract subscribers who stay instead of ones who try.

widgets.title: Cancel anytime:
widgets.description: One click, from the account page, effective at the end of the paid period, no email to write and no call to make. State your policy this plainly right under the plans.

widgets.title: What makes subscribers stay
widgets.subtitle: A subscription page should promise the things that reduce churn, and only the ones you deliver. Six that matter.

items.title: A fast first win
items.description: Onboarding that gets the subscriber to the first result in the first session, before the second charge is even close.

items.title: A predictable rhythm
items.description: New value on a schedule people can anticipate. Irregular delivery reads as neglect, even when the total is the same.

items.title: Visible new value
items.description: A changelog, a "new this month" email, a badge in the library. Subscribers should never wonder what they paid for.

items.title: A pause option
items.description: Pausing keeps a subscriber who would otherwise cancel. Offer it before the cancel button, not instead of it.

items.title: Transparent billing
items.description: A reminder before every renewal, receipts that explain themselves, no price change without notice.

items.title: An exit without friction
items.description: Cancelling in one click is the strongest reason to sign up in the first place. Make it true and say it.

widgets.title: Subscribe, receive, manage
widgets.subtitle: Three steps, so the visitor knows what happens after the button and how they stay in control.

items.title: Subscribe
items.description: Pick monthly or yearly, pay once, get immediate access. The confirmation email says when the next charge is.

items.title: Receive
items.description: New value arrives on the promised rhythm; the library grows; the "new this month" email keeps it visible.

items.title: Manage
items.description: Switch plans, pause or cancel from the account page. Every change takes effect at the end of the paid period.

widgets.title: Questions people ask before they subscribe
widgets.subtitle: Billing, cancellation and value questions, answered before checkout. The same answers feed a FAQ rich result in search.

items.title: What makes a subscription landing page different from a pricing page?
items.description: A pricing page compares plans for people who already decided to buy. A subscription landing page has to sell the recurring relationship first: what arrives every month, why it stays valuable, and how easy it is to leave.

items.title: Monthly or yearly first?
items.description: Show both, highlight yearly, and state the saving in plain units ("2 months free"), not percentages. Let the monthly price anchor the value before the yearly discount lands.

items.title: How prominent should the cancellation policy be?
items.description: As prominent as the price. "Cancel anytime, in one click, from your account" next to the plans removes the main fear of subscribing and costs nothing if you mean it.

items.title: Should I offer a free trial or a money-back window?
items.description: One of the two. A trial suits products people need to use to understand; a refund window suits content or services. Either way, say it once, near the price, and honour it without friction.

items.title: What keeps subscribers from churning?
items.description: What the retention section below lists: a fast first win, a predictable delivery rhythm, visible new value, a pause option and transparent billing. The landing page should promise only the ones you deliver.
